source_evidence: A high-yield corporate bond is a type of corporate bond that offers a higher rate of interest because of its higher risk of default.
answer: High-yield corporate bonds offer higher interest rates because they carry a higher risk of default. Issuers with greater estimated default risk may not qualify for an investment-grade credit rating, so they may offer higher interest to attract investors and compensate them for taking on that added risk. The higher rate and higher default risk are linked tradeoffs.
